propositions: plan-review passes write cache on every call and never read it across calls because the system prompt breakpoint is positioned after pass-specific content that varies per call, not at the shared plan-prefix boundary

within a single plan-review run, the finder pass writes a cache that subsequent verifier passes (Pass-2/verifier/prereq-verifier) should read but cannot because the breakpoint sits after their individual stance suffixes, not after the shared prefix

across different tickets, the marked prefix deliberately embeds the whole plan text (by design for within-run reuse), so cross-ticket cache hits are impossible and the apparent instability is a consequence of content-addressed caching, not a defect

the cost per leaf review is ~9.2-9.5k premium-rate cache-write tokens with zero reads, wasting 5-6k token-equivalents that could be saved by relocating the cache breakpoint to the shared-prefix boundary

the telemetry diagnostic warn_if_cache_ineffective only flags write==0 AND read==0 cases, so it cannot detect the write-every-call/read-never shape and this class of waste is invisible to current observability

the fix requires splitting the system prompt (static shared prefix + dynamic pass-specific suffix) so pydantic-ai places the cache breakpoint at the shared boundary, enabling within-run reads by verifier passes and same-ticket re-reviews within the TTL
